audit.whatIsWrong: Both charts read Skill/Skill/Skill/Heimerdinger/Skill/Heimerdinger/Heimerdinger while the whys[] beside them said the opposite on four rows — 'turret wall, rockets, and stun zone you off the lane at level 1' sat on a Skill row, and 'Level 4 is a skill check' sat on a Heimerdinger row.
audit.why: The mirror (heimerdinger__sett) settled the chart as Heimerdinger / Heimerdinger / Skill / Skill / Skill / Heimerdinger / Skill. The packet chart agrees that levels 1-3 are Heimerdinger's and that first item is his.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 3 and 6 flipped in both layers as one atomic group, ratings moved to match, phase whys rewritten, and whys[6] de-claimed so the late game no longer promises a win on a Skill row.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown or range appeared anywhere, and the first-item spike described UPGRADE!!! as if it permanently improved his turrets.
audit.why: CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade is a flat 11s at 970 range — it never gets shorter, which is what makes baiting it a reliable plan. Micro-Rockets are 11/10/9/8/7s at 1325 range. UPGRADE!!! is 100/85/70s and, per Riot's text, empowers his NEXT spell rather than upgrading the turret line permanently.
audit.corrected: Grenade's flat 11s and 970 range keyed to the level-2, level-3 and level-6 lines; rocket range and cadence added to the cooldown block; UPGRADE!!! restated as a 100s next-spell empower.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two errors. (a) breakdown.cooldowns names an ability that does not exist: 'CH-3X Lightning Grenade'. Heimerdinger's E is CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade. (b) Facebreaker is called an 'E stun' throughout, with no mention that it stuns only when enemies are on opposite sides of Sett — approaching a lone Heimerdinger behind a turret line, it is a slow.
audit.why: packet.enemyAbilities and the kit file both give E = CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade; 'CH-3X Lightning Grenade' is a fabricated name sitting in the block the player is told to track. Riot's Sett E text: 'If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned.' The mirror recorded the same Facebreaker point and the same Haymaker centre-true-damage rule.
audit.corrected: Fabricated name replaced with the real one and the block rewritten with real numbers; the two-sided condition on Facebreaker written into spikes[0] and spikes[3], with the Haymaker centre cash stated in the level-6 spike.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page's headline advice is 'build MR' and its common-mistakes row says 'Stack pure HP' — but nothing tells the player the actual reason the approach fails, which is range and the flat-cooldown stun, not damage type.
audit.why: Sett has no dash. Rockets reach 1325 and the grenade 970 against a 490-range pull and a 400-range ult; the lane is lost on approach, not on resistances.
audit.corrected: Level-1 and 2+ items phase whys now state the range problem and that R is a 400-range cast you must close to, rather than repeating a resistance recommendation.

edits.before: Double-punch passive makes you the strongest level-1 auto-trader in the lane. Punish Heimerdinger on every CS, but respect his opening tool — chips now, all-ins later.
edits.after: Heimerdinger walls you off at 1 — turrets for 20 mana, rockets from 1325 range, and you have no dash to answer with. Give up the CS, dodge, and bank the chip as Grit.

edits.before: Q gives move speed toward Heimerdinger and two empowered punches. Take short Q trades and back off before he can answer with CH-2 Grenade (Stun).
edits.after: A second turret pins you behind the wave. His grenade is a flat 11s at 970 range — that is the cooldown to bait before you spend anything of your own.

edits.before: Q ranks make your punch trades heavier, but Heimerdinger has his core tools too. Keep the grit bar honest: trade in, W-shield his return damage, out.
edits.after: Q ranks make your punch trades heavier, but the turret line does his work for him. Reach him through it and you burst him; whiff the approach and you get poked out.

edits.before: Sterak's makes your all-in nearly unburstable. Fights are decided by whether you cash a max-grit W — track CH-2 Grenade (Stun) and commit on the gap.
edits.after: Sterak's makes your all-in nearly unburstable. It comes down to whether you reach him at all — R is a 400-range cast, so close past the turrets first.

edits.before: - Heimerdinger CH-2 Grenade (Stun): matchup-defining — His self-peel stun. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Heimerdinger CH-3X Lightning Grenade: Lobs a grenade that slows, and stuns at the center. Dodge or sidestep it.
edits.after: - Heimerdinger CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade: matchup-defining — a flat 11s at 970 range, stunning a direct hit and slowing around it. Bait it before you commit. - Heimerdinger Hextech Micro-Rockets: 1325-range poke, 7s at rank 5. Sidestep it.

edits.before: Late game your R and items flip past the turret wall to burst a squishy Heimer.
edits.after: Late game hinges on reaching him past the turret wall before he pokes you out.

edits.before: Turrets (Q) plus his W rockets and E stun wall you off — with E Facebreaker, wait for his E Grenade to miss, then commit through the turret zone and pull him for a Q-W burst.
edits.after: H-28 G Evolution Turret plus Hextech Micro-Rockets wall you off. Wait for CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade (11s) to miss, then commit through the turret zone and pull him across your minions.

edits.before: Your R The Show Stopper is the answer — flip Heimerdinger over his own turret line and dump W, ideally after his E stun is spent so he can't peel the all-in.
edits.after: The Show Stopper is the answer — carry him back over his own turret line, then cash Haymaker with him dead-centre. Spend it after his grenade (11s), never into it.

edits.before: He tips back ahead: his R-upgraded turrets and rocket poke let him zone and chunk you before you close, so wait to dive until his E Grenade is on cooldown.
edits.after: He tips back ahead: UPGRADE!!! (100s) empowers his next spell, and rocket poke zones you before you can close — dive only once the grenade (11s) is spent.

edits.before: You come back online — with items and R you can flip past the turret wall and burst him, since he's squishy the instant you land your E stun and W.
edits.after: Late is decided by the approach — Facebreaker stuns only with a target on each side, so pull him across a minion or his own turret, then cash Haymaker on his centre.

edits.before: Heimerdinger dominates levels 1-3 — his turret wall, W rockets, and E stun zone you off the wave entirely, so give up some CS, dodge the Grenade, and stack Grit off the chip.
edits.after: Heimerdinger owns levels 1-3 — his turret line, Hextech Micro-Rockets and the Electron Storm Grenade zone you off the wave, so give up CS, dodge the grenade, and bank the chip as Grit.

edits.before: With items and R you flip past his turret line and one-combo him since he's squishy — respect his E stun, but a landed engage ends the fight in your favor.
edits.after: Items and R let you reach past the turret line, but you get one attempt — the Electron Storm Grenade stuns a direct hit, and a missed engage leaves you poked out of the fight.

notes: A fabricated ability name was sitting in the cooldown block the player is told to track: 'CH-3X Lightning Grenade'. The real name is CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade; it is now used, with the flat 11s cooldown and 970 range. The packet defect ('never names any of Heimerdinger's abilities') is addressed in the content layer and the cooldown block, but the full layer's focus.text, tldr, loading and every dos/donts row still read 'CH-2 Grenade (Stun)', a made-up short form rather than the real name — those are short enum-ish strings scattered across a dozen paths and need one coordinated rename rather than piecemeal edits. One thing I did not assert: whether Sett's Facebreaker counts a deployed turret as the 'enemy on the opposite side' that converts the slow into a stun. Riot's text says 'all enemies' without defining it, so the advice says a minion or his turret without claiming which one works.
